messages:
samir: quick dump of the sim results for the slab wear-leveling idea — posting raw numbers first so we can iterate.

maria: thanks, pls include the perf counters you used.

samir: pasted below. basic setup: 4k active keys, skewed tail (zipf s=1.2), long-context workload generating 1.2M tokens over 30m. allocator=power_of_two (base 256B), slab buckets: [256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192].

samir: baseline (no compaction):
- resident delta: +1.9GB over 30m
- observed fragmentation (lost_to_internal / total_cache): 18%
- mean latency p95: +6ms vs no-cache case (due to working set pressure)

kai: those numbers track with what I saw in last replay. what about CPU?

samir: CPU stable, ~3% extra sys due to kmalloc paths. but GC/major compaction would spike.

samir: experiment A — smaller base block (128B) + finer buckets:
- resident delta: +1.1GB (improved)
- fragmentation: 11%
- CPU: +5% steady (alloc hot path heavier)
- p95: neutral

maria: so lower mem at cost of CPU. tradeoff looks acceptable for hosted nodes where we care about OOMs. any perf regression in tail latency?

samir: none observed in p99.3, but jitter in p95 increased slightly under bursty sequences.

jonathan: can we do dynamic bucket resizing? e.g., keep 256B normally, temporarily insert 128B for heavy long-context streams then revert.

samir: we simulated that (Experiment B — adaptive base):
- when long-context flag true -> promote 128B buckets for that connection only
- mem delta over baseline: +0.6GB improvement vs baseline
- complexity: adds per-conn state and slightly more fragmentation churn after revert

maria: how invasive is the per-conn state change? would it affect the common hot path?

samir: minimal. we keep LRU per-slab as today; per-conn bucket preference is a pointer in the session struct. alloc path checks it (fast path uses branch).

kai: okay, but I'm worried about allocator wear: frequent promote/revert will cause repeated free/alloc pattern and fragmentation reappears. Did you try compaction?

samir: yes. Experiment C — background incremental compaction (proto):
config snippet:
```
kv_cache_compaction: {
  mode: "incremental",
  stride_bytes: 64k,
  interval_ms: 250,
  threshold_frag_pct: 12
}
```
results:
- resident delta: +0.4GB vs baseline
- fragmentation: ~6%
- CPU: +2% in background threads
- tail pauses: <2ms observed during copy phases (we used non-blocking remap API)

jonathan: nice. where is the copy happening — user thread or bg thread?

samir: dedicated bg worker per node, uses async appends and page remap when possible. falls back to memcpy for partial pages.

maria: any atomicity/consistency concerns for KV lookups during a tile compaction window?

samir: we use versioned pointers + CAS swap at bucket granularity. lookups see either old or new location; we keep tombstones for a short grace period. compaction cleans tombstones later.

kai: can you share the profiler flame for compaction worker? build-bot uploaded the run: 1783001500.

build-bot: uploaded profile: https://ci.internal/reports/1783001500/compaction-flame.svg :thumbsup: 

samir: tl;dr from flame: most time in memcpy when fallback is needed; mmap remap path cheap. we should align compaction stride to page boundaries to avoid memcpy.

maria: any regression risk on Dedicated customers who have pinned kernels? kernel remap calls might not be available on older distros.

samir: fallback memcpy handles that; but we should gate remap behind a capability check and keep a safe default (interval_ms=1000, stride=16k).

jonathan: interesting thought — what about a hybrid: wear-leveling allocator + opportunistic compaction only when node idle (low QPS)?

samir: Experiment D (opportunistic): compaction runs only when avg CPU<20% and tail qps<10%. results: similar mem wins to incremental but almost zero CPU impact and near-zero tail jitter. downside: depends on idle periods, so not reliable in 24/7 high throughput clusters.

maria: proposal summary?
samir: proposal for RFC:
- default: keep base 256B, add config knob for base=128B for memory critical fleets
- implement 'adaptive base' per-connection as opt-in (feature flag)
- implement background incremental compaction with remap fallback, stride/page-aligned by default
- add opportunistic mode for low-util fleets
- telemetry: expose fragmentation pct, compaction cycles, memcpy fallback count, compaction cpu secs

kai: +1 to telemetry. would like a kill-switch in case compaction causes unforeseen tail regressions.

maria: timeline?

samir: proto in PR today for compaction worker + config (small patch). hoping for bench infra runs next week, then dogfood on staging for 2 weeks.

jonathan: please include a failing-case test that simulates constant long-context high-QPS so we can ensure opportunistic doesn’t claim wins in prod.

samir: will do. next: I'll open RFC with numbers and prototype code pointers. cc @maria @kai for review.

maria: thanks — looks actionable. :rocket:
